question: Which is the largest planet of the solar system?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Jupiter.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Jupiter is the largest planet in the solar system. Its diameter is about 1,42,984 km, roughly 11 times that of the Earth, and its mass is more than twice that of all the other planets combined. (बृहस्पति — सौरमंडल का सबसे बड़ा ग्रह)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Jupiter is a gas giant made mostly of hydrogen and helium; its famous Great Red Spot is a giant storm that has raged for centuries.

• It has the most moons among the planets; the four largest — Io, Europa, Ganymede and Callisto — were discovered by Galileo in 1610 and are called the Galilean moons. Ganymede is the largest moon in the solar system.

• Order of planets by size (largest to smallest): Jupiter > Saturn > Uranus > Neptune > Earth > Venus > Mars > Mercury.

NOTE

• Other quick facts: Mercury is the smallest and closest to the Sun; Venus is the hottest planet; Saturn is famous for its rings and is the least dense planet; Neptune is the farthest planet from the Sun.

question: Who is the author of the book titled 'Fearless Governance'?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kiran Bedi.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Fearless Governance" was written by Dr. Kiran Bedi, India's first woman IPS officer and former Lieutenant Governor of Puducherry. The book draws on her experience in policing and administration. (निडर शासन — किरण बेदी)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Kiran Bedi joined the IPS in 1972, served as Inspector General of Tihar Jail (where her reforms won the Ramon Magsaysay Award, 1994), and was awarded the Padma Shri.

• Her other books include "It's Always Possible", "I Dare!" and "As I See...".

NOTE

• Other authors in the options: Amitav Ghosh (The Shadow Lines, The Hungry Tide, Gun Island — Jnanpith Award winner), Anuj Dhar (India's Biggest Cover-up, on Netaji), Anirudh Suri (The Great Tech Game).

question: There are regions where farmers specialise in vegetables only. This type of farming is known as ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Truck farming.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Truck farming" is the type of market gardening in which farmers specialise only in growing vegetables for nearby urban markets. The name comes from the old English word "truck", meaning barter/exchange of goods, and also from the trucks used to carry vegetables to market. (ट्रक कृषि — केवल सब्ज़ियों की खेती)

• The distance of such farms from the market is often governed by how far a truck can travel overnight.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Mixed farming = growing crops and rearing livestock on the same farm.

• Pastoral farming = rearing of animals (sheep, cattle) on grasslands, without crop cultivation.

• Dairy farming = rearing of milch animals for milk and milk products.

NOTE

• Related terms: Market gardening/Horticulture (intensive cultivation of vegetables, fruits and flowers near cities), Plantation agriculture (single cash crop like tea, coffee, rubber), Shifting cultivation (Jhum) and Intensive subsistence farming.

question: Tensile or compressive stress can also be termed as _________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is longitudinal stress.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• When a deforming force acts along the length (the longitudinal axis) of a body, the restoring force per unit area is called longitudinal stress. It is of two kinds:

◦ Tensile stress — when the body is stretched (its length increases).

◦ Compressive stress — when the body is squeezed (its length decreases).

• Hence tensile or compressive stress is collectively termed longitudinal stress. (अनुदैर्ध्य प्रतिबल)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Tangential (shearing) stress acts parallel to the surface and changes the shape of the body without changing its volume.

• Hydraulic (volumetric/bulk) stress acts normally and uniformly on the whole surface (as in a fluid) and changes the volume of the body.

• Stress = Force / Area; its SI unit is N/m² (pascal, Pa).

NOTE

• Hooke's Law: within the elastic limit, stress ∝ strain, and stress/strain = modulus of elasticity.

◦ Young's modulus (Y) — longitudinal stress/longitudinal strain.

◦ Bulk modulus (K) — hydraulic stress/volume strain.

◦ Modulus of rigidity (η) — shearing stress/shearing strain.

question: Panthi dance form is associated with ________ state of India.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Chhattisgarh.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Panthi" is a well-known folk dance of Chhattisgarh, performed by the Satnami community on Maghi Purnima, the birth anniversary of their spiritual leader Guru Ghasidas. (पंथी नृत्य — छत्तीसगढ़)

• The dancers perform around a jaitkhamb (a sacred pillar), singing songs of devotion and nirvana, and the tempo grows faster as the dance progresses, often ending in acrobatic pyramids.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Other folk dances of Chhattisgarh: Raut Nacha, Karma, Saila, Panthi, Pandwani (a folk ballad form popularised by Teejan Bai).

• Folk dances of the other options: Kerala — Kaikottikali, Ottamthullal, Theyyam; Maharashtra — Lavani, Tamasha, Dhangari Gaja; Punjab — Bhangra, Giddha.

NOTE

• Classical vs folk: India has 8 classical dances (Bharatanatyam, Kathak, Kathakali, Kuchipudi, Odissi, Manipuri, Mohiniyattam, Sattriya), while folk dances are region- and community-specific.

question:
Which of the following referred to as 'paper taxes'?

I. Wealth tax

II. Gift tax
solution_text:
The correct answer is Both I and II.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Wealth tax and Gift tax were together nicknamed "paper taxes" in India because they existed on paper (in the statute book) but yielded very little actual revenue, their collection cost and evasion being disproportionately high. (कागज़ी कर)

• Both were direct taxes recommended by the economist Nicholas Kaldor and introduced in 1957–58.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Gift Tax was introduced by the Gift Tax Act, 1958 and abolished in 1998.

• Wealth Tax was levied under the Wealth Tax Act, 1957 and abolished in the Union Budget 2015-16, being replaced by an additional surcharge on the super-rich.

• Estate duty (another Kaldor tax) was abolished in 1985.

NOTE

• Direct taxes (burden cannot be shifted): income tax, corporate tax, capital gains tax.

• Indirect taxes (burden shifted to the consumer): GST, customs duty, excise duty.

• Direct taxes in India are administered by the CBDT and indirect taxes by the CBIC, both under the Ministry of Finance.

question: The Buddha belonged to a small gana known as ______ .
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sakya gana.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Gautama Buddha (Siddhartha) was born into the Sakya (Shakya) gana/sangha, a small republican clan whose capital was Kapilavastu. His father Suddhodana was the elected chief of the Sakyas. (शाक्य गण)

• Because of this, the Buddha is also called "Sakyamuni" — the sage of the Sakyas.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The Buddha was born at Lumbini (Nepal) in 563 BCE, attained enlightenment at Bodh Gaya, gave his first sermon (Dharmachakra Pravartana) at Sarnath, and attained Mahaparinirvana at Kushinagar.

• Ganas/Sanghas were republics (oligarchies) of the 6th century BCE, such as the Sakyas of Kapilavastu, the Lichchhavis of Vaishali and the Mallas of Kushinagar/Pava, in contrast to monarchies like Magadha and Kosala.

NOTE

• Avanti (capital Ujjain/Mahishmati), Kuru (capital Indraprastha/Hastinapur) and Panchala (capital Ahichchhatra/Kampilya) were Mahajanapadas, not the Buddha's clan.

question: Jayanthi Kumaresh is one of the foremost exponents of _______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is veena.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Dr. Jayanthi Kumaresh is one of India's foremost exponents of the Saraswati Veena, a leading name in Carnatic instrumental music. (वीणा वादिका — जयंती कुमरेश)

• She comes from a family of musicians (the Lalgudi–Jayaraman lineage) and has performed worldwide, blending traditional Carnatic veena with collaborative and fusion projects.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The veena is one of the oldest Indian string instruments, associated with Goddess Saraswati; its Carnatic form is the Saraswati veena and the Hindustani form is the Rudra veena.

• Other famous veena players: S. Balachander, Chitti Babu, E. Gayathri, Doraiswamy Iyengar.

NOTE

• Exponents of the other instruments: Santoor — Pt. Shivkumar Sharma, Bhajan Sopori; Tabla — Ustad Zakir Hussain, Pt. Kishan Maharaj, Ustad Alla Rakha; Sitar — Pt. Ravi Shankar, Ustad Vilayat Khan, Anoushka Shankar.

question: The Chhath Puja festival is dedicated to the ______ God.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sun.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Chhath Puja is dedicated to the Sun God (Surya) and his consort Chhathi Maiya (Usha). Devotees offer "arghya" (water offerings) to the setting and rising sun while standing in a river or pond, praying for the well-being and prosperity of their family. (छठ पूजा — सूर्य देव)

• It is celebrated mainly in Bihar, Jharkhand, eastern Uttar Pradesh and Nepal, on the sixth day (Shashthi) of the Kartika month.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The festival involves a rigorous four-day ritual — Nahay Khay, Kharna, Sandhya Arghya and Usha Arghya — including a waterless fast (nirjala vrat) of about 36 hours.

• Chhath is considered one of the few Vedic festivals still observed, requiring no priest; the devotee (vrati) performs the rituals personally.

NOTE

• Other sun-related festivals: Makar Sankranti, Pongal, Magh Bihu (harvest festivals marking the sun's northward journey — Uttarayan) and the Konark Sun Temple (Odisha), a UNESCO World Heritage Site dedicated to Surya.

question: Barakar is the tributary of which of the following rivers?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Damodar.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Barakar is the largest and most important tributary of the Damodar river. It rises near Padma in the Hazaribagh district of Jharkhand and joins the Damodar near Dishergarh (West Bengal). (बराकर — दामोदर की सहायक नदी)

• The famous Maithon Dam is built on the Barakar under the Damodar Valley Corporation (DVC).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The Damodar rises in the Chotanagpur plateau (Palamu hills, Jharkhand) and joins the Hooghly in West Bengal. It was historically called the "Sorrow of Bengal" because of its devastating floods.

• The Damodar Valley Corporation (1948) was India's first multipurpose river valley project, modelled on the Tennessee Valley Authority (TVA) of the USA. Its dams include Tilaiya, Konar, Maithon and Panchet.

NOTE

• Tributaries of the other rivers: Kaveri — Hemavati, Kabini, Bhavani, Amaravati; Krishna — Bhima, Tungabhadra, Koyna, Ghataprabha; Ravi — Budhil, Nai/Dhona, Siul, Ujh.

question: The famous Sheesh Mahal in Punjab was built by which of the following rulers?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Maharaja Narinder Singh.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The famous Sheesh Mahal at Patiala (Punjab) was built by Maharaja Narinder Singh of Patiala in the mid-19th century (around 1847). (शीश महल, पटियाला — महाराजा नरिंदर सिंह)

• It is part of the Moti Bagh Palace complex and is renowned for its mirror work, frescoes and the adjoining Lakshman Jhula bridge; it today houses a museum with a large collection of medals.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Maharaja Sawai Pratap Singh of Jaipur built the Hawa Mahal (1799).

• Rana Kumbha of Mewar built the Kumbhalgarh Fort and the Vijay Stambha at Chittorgarh.

• Raja Man Singh I of Amber was a general of Akbar and built the Amber Fort palace complex.

NOTE

• "Sheesh Mahal" (Palace of Mirrors) structures also exist at Agra Fort, Lahore Fort, Amber Fort and Shalimar Bagh, all noted for shish (mirror) inlay work.

question: Article ______ of the Indian constitution provides for superintendence, direction and control of elections vested in an Election commission.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 324.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Article 324 of the Constitution vests the superintendence, direction and control of elections to Parliament, the State Legislatures, and the offices of the President and Vice-President in the Election Commission of India (ECI). (अनुच्छेद 324 — निर्वाचन आयोग)

• The ECI was established on 25 January 1950, now celebrated as National Voters' Day.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Part XV (Articles 324–329) of the Constitution deals with elections:

◦ Article 325 — no person to be ineligible for inclusion in the electoral roll on grounds of religion, race, caste or sex.

◦ Article 326 — elections on the basis of adult suffrage (voting age reduced from 21 to 18 by the 61st Amendment, 1988).

◦ Article 327/328 — power of Parliament/State Legislature to make laws on elections.

◦ Article 329 — bar to interference by courts in electoral matters.

NOTE

• Other options: Article 330 — reservation of seats for SCs/STs in the Lok Sabha; Article 336 — special provision for the Anglo-Indian community in certain services; Article 338 — National Commission for Scheduled Castes.

• The ECI is a multi-member body (currently a Chief Election Commissioner and two Election Commissioners).

question: Which class of algae is commonly known as brown algae?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Phaeophyceae.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The class Phaeophyceae is commonly known as brown algae. Their brown colour is due to the presence of the pigment "fucoxanthin" along with chlorophyll a and c. (भूरे शैवाल)

• They are mostly marine, store food as laminarin and mannitol, and their cell walls contain cellulose with algin.

• Examples: Laminaria, Fucus, Sargassum, Ectocarpus, Dictyota.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Chlorophyceae — green algae: pigments chlorophyll a and b; stored food starch; e.g., Chlamydomonas, Spirogyra, Ulva, Volvox.

• Rhodophyceae — red algae: pigment r-phycoerythrin; stored food floridean starch; e.g., Polysiphonia, Gelidium, Gracilaria (source of agar).

• Chrysophyceae includes diatoms and golden algae.

NOTE

• Economic uses: agar (from red algae) is used in culture media and ice cream; algin (from brown algae) is used as a thickener; Chlorella is a protein-rich food supplement used even in space missions.

question: The Constitution (Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes) Orders Bills 2022 was introduced in ______ state of India.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Jharkhand.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Constitution (Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes) Orders (Amendment) Bill, 2022 related to Jharkhand. It sought to amend the lists of Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes of the state — notably including the Bhogta and other communities among the Scheduled Tribes of Jharkhand. (झारखंड)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Under Article 341, the President specifies the Scheduled Castes of a State/UT, and under Article 342 the Scheduled Tribes — in consultation with the Governor.

• Any inclusion in or exclusion from these lists can only be done by an Act of Parliament, not by a later presidential notification.

NOTE

• Jharkhand was carved out of Bihar on 15 November 2000 (birth anniversary of Birsa Munda) and has a large tribal population — major tribes include Santhal, Oraon, Munda, Ho and Kharia.

question: Which among the following Indian Olympians is associated with wrestling sport?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sakshi Malik.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Sakshi Malik is an Indian wrestler who won a bronze medal in the 58 kg freestyle category at the 2016 Rio Olympics, becoming the first Indian woman wrestler to win an Olympic medal. (साक्षी मलिक — कुश्ती)

• She hails from Rohtak, Haryana, and has also won gold at the 2022 Commonwealth Games (Birmingham).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Neeraj Chopra — javelin throw; gold at the Tokyo 2020 Olympics (India's first Olympic gold in athletics) and World Championship gold (2023).

• Abhinav Bindra — 10 m air rifle shooting; India's first individual Olympic gold medallist (Beijing 2008).

• Aditi Ashok — golf; finished a memorable fourth at the Tokyo Olympics.

NOTE

• Other Indian Olympic medal-winning wrestlers: K. D. Jadhav (1952 — India's first individual Olympic medal), Sushil Kumar (2008, 2012), Yogeshwar Dutt (2012), Bajrang Punia (2020) and Ravi Kumar Dahiya (2020 silver).

question: Who wrote the novel "Life of Pi"?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Yann Martel.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Life of Pi" (2001) was written by the Canadian author Yann Martel. It won the prestigious Man Booker Prize in 2002. (यान मार्टेल)

• The novel tells the story of Piscine "Pi" Patel, a boy from Puducherry (Pondicherry), India, who survives 227 days adrift in the Pacific Ocean on a lifeboat with a Bengal tiger named Richard Parker.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The book was adapted into an acclaimed 2012 film directed by Ang Lee, which won four Academy Awards, including Best Director.

• Other authors listed: Jonathan Safran Foer (Everything Is Illuminated), Khaled Hosseini (The Kite Runner, A Thousand Splendid Suns), Carol Birch (Jamrach's Menagerie).

NOTE

• Indian-origin Booker Prize winners: V. S. Naipaul (1971), Salman Rushdie (1981 — Midnight's Children), Arundhati Roy (1997 — The God of Small Things), Kiran Desai (2006 — The Inheritance of Loss), Aravind Adiga (2008 — The White Tiger).

question: The colour of the alluvial soils varies from ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is light grey to ash grey.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The colour of alluvial soil varies from light grey to ash grey, depending on the depth of deposition, the texture of the material and the time taken for maturity. (जलोढ़ मिट्टी — हल्के धूसर से राख जैसे धूसर रंग की)

• Alluvial soil is deposited by rivers and is the most widespread and most fertile soil of India, covering about 40% of the total land area, chiefly the Northern Plains and the coastal deltas.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Alluvial soils are rich in potash, phosphoric acid and lime but deficient in nitrogen and humus. They are ideal for wheat, rice, sugarcane and pulses.

• They are classified as Khadar (newer, lighter, more fertile, flood-renewed) and Bhangar (older, darker, containing kankar or lime nodules).

NOTE

• Other soils of India: Black (Regur) soil — dark, ideal for cotton, formed from Deccan lava; Red and Yellow soil — reddish due to iron diffusion; Laterite soil — formed by intense leaching in high rainfall areas; Desert soil and Mountain/Forest soil.

question: When was the Dev Samaj founded in Lahore by Shiv Narayan Agnihotri?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1887.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Dev Samaj was founded at Lahore in 1887 by Pandit Shiv Narayan Agnihotri, a former Brahmo Samaj follower. (देव समाज — 1887, लाहौर)

• The Samaj emphasised the eternity of the soul, the supremacy of the guru, and a moral/ethical way of life; it opposed child marriage and campaigned for social reform and women's education.

• Its teachings were compiled in the book "Dev Shastra".

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Agnihotri, originally named Shiv Narayan, took the name Dev Guru Bhagwan and was regarded as a "deva purusha" by his followers.

• The Samaj founded the Dev Samaj College for Women at Ferozepur (1934), a pioneering institution for women's education.

NOTE

• Other reform movements and their years: Brahmo Samaj — 1828 (Raja Ram Mohan Roy), Prarthana Samaj — 1867 (Atmaram Pandurang), Arya Samaj — 1875 (Swami Dayanand Saraswati), Theosophical Society — 1875 (Blavatsky & Olcott), Ramakrishna Mission — 1897 (Swami Vivekananda).

question: Sangam poems mention a tamil word 'Muvendar' which means ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Three chiefs.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Tamil word "Muvendar" mentioned in the Sangam poems means "three chiefs". It refers to the heads of the three ruling families of ancient Tamilakam — the Cholas, Cheras and Pandyas. (मुवेंदर — तीन मुखिया)

• These chiefs controlled the region from about the second century BCE, each maintaining two power centres — one inland and one on the coast.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Capitals/ports: Chola — Uraiyur (inland) and Puhar/Kaveripattinam (port); Chera — Vanji and the port of Muziris (Muchiri); Pandya — Madurai and the port of Korkai.

• The Sangam Age (roughly 300 BCE – 300 CE) produced the earliest Tamil literature — Tolkappiyam, Ettuthogai, Pattuppattu, Silappadikaram and Manimekalai.

NOTE

• Emblems: Chola — tiger, Chera — bow, Pandya — fish. The Sangams were assemblies of Tamil poets held under royal patronage, traditionally at Madurai.

question: According to the 2011 census, what is the male literacy rate?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 82.14%.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• According to the Census of India 2011, the male literacy rate was 82.14%, while the female literacy rate was 65.46% and the overall literacy rate was 74.04%. (2011 जनगणना — पुरुष साक्षरता 82.14%)

• A "literate" person in the census is one aged 7 years and above who can both read and write with understanding in any language.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The 2011 Census was the 15th national census and the 7th after independence; its motto was "Our Census, Our Future".

• Kerala had the highest literacy rate (93.91%) and Bihar the lowest (61.80%); Lakshadweep was the most literate UT.

• Total population (2011): 121.08 crore; sex ratio: 943 females per 1000 males; density: 382 persons/km².

NOTE

• The literacy gender gap narrowed from about 21.6 percentage points in 2001 to 16.68 in 2011. Census operations are conducted under the Census Act, 1948, by the Registrar General and Census Commissioner of India (Ministry of Home Affairs).

question: In January 2022, S Somanath has been appointed as the tenth chairman of ________ .
solution_text:
The correct answer is ISRO.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In January 2022, the eminent rocket scientist Shri S. Somanath was appointed the tenth Chairman of the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO), succeeding Dr. K. Sivan. He is also Secretary, Department of Space. (एस. सोमनाथ — इसरो के दसवें अध्यक्ष)

• Before this he headed the Vikram Sarabhai Space Centre (VSSC), Thiruvananthapuram, and is known for his work on the GSLV Mk-III (LVM3) launch vehicle.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• ISRO was established on 15 August 1969; its headquarters is at Bengaluru and its founder was Dr. Vikram Sarabhai, regarded as the father of the Indian space programme.

• Under Somanath's leadership ISRO achieved the historic Chandrayaan-3 soft landing near the lunar south pole (23 August 2023) and launched Aditya-L1, India's first solar mission.

NOTE

• Related organisations: RBI (central bank, est. 1935, HQ Mumbai), DRDO (defence research, est. 1958, HQ New Delhi), SEBI (securities market regulator, statutory in 1992, HQ Mumbai).

question: The equipment 'Shuttlecock' is required in which sports?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Badminton.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "shuttlecock" (also called the shuttle or birdie) is the projectile used in badminton. It has an open conical crown of feathers (or synthetic material) fixed to a rounded cork base. (बैडमिंटन — शटलकॉक)

• A standard feather shuttlecock has 16 feathers and weighs about 4.74–5.50 g.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Badminton is governed by the Badminton World Federation (BWF); the court measures 13.4 m × 6.1 m (singles width 5.18 m) and the net height at the centre is 1.524 m.

• Major badminton tournaments: Thomas Cup (men's team), Uber Cup (women's team), All England Open, Sudirman Cup. India won the Thomas Cup in 2022 for the first time.

• Indian stars: Prakash Padukone, Pullela Gopichand, Saina Nehwal, P. V. Sindhu, Lakshya Sen, Satwiksairaj Rankireddy–Chirag Shetty.

NOTE

• Equipment of the other sports: Basketball — basket, backboard; Billiards — cue, cue ball, table; Baseball — bat, mitt, diamond, home plate.

question: What was the objective of "Arya Samaj" founded by "Swami Dayanand Saraswati"?
option_3: To encourage the practice of barter trade
solution_text:
The correct answer is To reform Hinduism.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Arya Samaj, founded by Swami Dayanand Saraswati at Bombay in 1875, aimed at reforming Hinduism by purging it of idol worship, caste rigidity, untouchability, child marriage and priestly domination, and returning to the pure teachings of the Vedas. (आर्य समाज — हिंदू धर्म का सुधार)

• Its famous slogan was "Back to the Vedas"; Dayanand's major work was "Satyarth Prakash".

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The Arya Samaj promoted widow remarriage, women's education, inter-caste marriage and the Shuddhi movement (reconversion to Hinduism).

• It set up the DAV (Dayanand Anglo-Vedic) schools and colleges (first at Lahore, 1886) and, under Swami Shraddhanand, the Gurukul at Kangri (1902).

NOTE

• Swami Dayanand Saraswati (1824–1883), born Mool Shankar in Tankara, Gujarat, was the first to give the call of "Swaraj" — India for Indians — later echoed by Tilak.

question: The process by which two immiscible liquids, get mixed while one disperses as small droplets within the other is known as ________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Emulsification.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Emulsification" is the process in which two immiscible liquids are mixed so that one is dispersed as fine droplets throughout the other, forming an emulsion. (पायसीकरण)

◦ Examples: milk (fat droplets dispersed in water), butter, mayonnaise, and oil-and-vinegar salad dressings.

• Substances that stabilise an emulsion are called emulsifiers/emulsifying agents — e.g., soap, detergents, lecithin (in egg yolk) and casein (in milk).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Separation is a general term for splitting a mixture into its components.

• Caramelisation is the browning of sugar on heating, which gives caramel its colour and flavour.

• Filtration separates insoluble solids from a liquid using a filter medium.

NOTE

• Two types of emulsions: oil-in-water (o/w) — milk, mayonnaise; and water-in-oil (w/o) — butter, cold cream.

• Emulsification is also how bile salts in the human body break fat into small droplets so that the enzyme lipase can digest it.

question: History of Akbar's reign, titled "Akbar Nama" is written by ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Abul Fazl.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "Akbarnama", the official history of Emperor Akbar's reign, was written in Persian by Abul Fazl, one of the Navaratnas (nine gems) of Akbar's court. (अकबरनामा — अबुल फज़ल)

• It is in three volumes: the first two narrate the history of Akbar's ancestors and his reign, while the third, the "Ain-i-Akbari", is a detailed statistical and administrative account of the empire — its provinces (subas), revenue, army (mansabdari), customs and culture.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Abd al-Qadir Badauni wrote "Muntakhab-ut-Tawarikh", a critical (often hostile) account of Akbar's religious policies.

• Abbas Khan Sherwani wrote "Tarikh-i-Sher Shahi", a history of Sher Shah Suri.

• Abul Fazl was killed in 1602 by Bir Singh Bundela at the instigation of Prince Salim (later Jahangir).

NOTE
